description: Composable melodic-techno devices. The club_drive profile prioritizes rhythmic propulsion and instrumental hooks; these remain editable starting points rather than fixed templates.

performance_profiles.groove: Keep a punchy four-on-the-floor kick through high-energy sections, place clap on beats two and four, use dark sixteenth hats and offbeat open hats, and give the mid-bass a syncopated eighth-note motor around a short, centered sub.
performance_profiles.lead: Build the hook from a fast-attack layered saw or pulse voice with a distinct upper harmonic layer. Give the lead a repeating 1–2 bar phrase, then vary its ending, octave, or filter at 8- or 16-bar boundaries. Keep piano, vocal-like pads, and long strings as supporting colors.
performance_profiles.arrangement: Use a short groove-led intro, first drop, low-end pullback, build with filter and percussion motion, second drop with a clear hook variation, then a mix-out. Add a one-beat drum or bass fill at phrase endings.
performance_profiles.mix: Keep kick and sub mono and separately voiced; sidechain the mid-bass and sustained hook enough to reveal each kick. Keep the bass attack audible on small speakers. Make the lead bright with harmonics and controlled saturation, then leave transient room for the kick.
guardrails: Do not add bass layers that duplicate the same rhythm and register.
Do not use sustained pads as the main source of movement.
At each drop, add or change a rhythmic or instrumental part, not only master gain.

performance_profiles.groove: Use a restrained kick, spacious percussion, sustained harmony, and long melodic phrases.
performance_profiles.lead: Favor expressive sustained synth, piano, flute, or vocal-like color over dense repeating instrumental riffs.
performance_profiles.arrangement: Preserve long breakdowns and gradual transitions.
performance_profiles.mix: Prioritize dynamic contrast and space; keep low end centered.

harmony.character: dark, yearning, then lifted by the major dominant
harmony.development: Hold one common tone across adjacent chords and resolve the raised leading tone by semitone.

harmony.character: more modal and plaintive, with a soft return
harmony.development: Favor inversions with shared tones; keep the top voice moving by step.
Use the bass descent as the main change; let the lead repeat with small rhythmic variation.
Treat the b2 as a brief color or passing tone; avoid sustaining it over every layer.

harmony.character: brief emotional opening inside a minor-key track
harmony.development: Use the relative-major chord as a section lift, then return to tonic with a clear bass resolution.

harmony.character: open and unresolved until the turnaround
harmony.development: Resolve the suspended fourth late in the phrase and reserve the full dominant for section returns.

parts.sub: short root notes with kick clearance

groove_devices.variation: Change hat velocity and remove one kick-facing bass note every 8 or 16 bars.

parts.bass: sixteenth-note pulse with rests at phrase boundaries
parts.sub: reinforce selected roots, not every bass hit
parts.percussion: short tom or wood accent answers

groove_devices.variation: Use velocity shape and a one-beat fill at the end of a 16-bar phrase.

parts.bass: short, accented eighth notes alternating root, fifth and chord tone
parts.sub: root anchors on selected strong beats, strictly mono
parts.lead: fast-attack instrumental hook with upper harmonics

groove_devices.variation: Use a sixteenth pickup or one-beat fill only at the end of an 8- or 16-bar phrase; return to the core motif immediately.

parts.kick: steady during drop, reduced in breakdown
parts.bass: offbeat notes and held phrase-ending note

groove_devices.variation: Keep the long lead note stable while the rhythm section changes underneath.

parts.kick: remove or reduce to a distant pulse
parts.low_end: sub out; optional quiet low drone
parts.motif: piano, flute, or lead in foreground

groove_devices.variation: Build back with one rhythmic layer at a time, then restore the kick and sub together at the drop.

phrase_devices.rules: Keep the first phrase recognizable; answer by changing only one of register, ending note, or rhythm.

phrase_devices.shape: long chord tone on a strong beat followed by a short connecting figure
phrase_devices.rules: Keep the anchor on a chord tone; use scale steps for the run and leave a breath before the next anchor.

phrase_devices.shape: repeat a motif in its original register, then reveal the answer one octave higher
phrase_devices.rules: Use only at a major section lift; preserve rhythm so the listener recognizes the idea.

phrase_devices.shape: hold a shared or suspended tone while the harmony changes beneath it
phrase_devices.rules: Choose a tone that is consonant or intentionally tense over both chords, then resolve on the next phrase.

phrase_devices.shape: repeat the same pitch contour with a changed onset pattern
phrase_devices.rules: Change a small number of attacks; retain the phrase's strongest accent and ending.

arrangement_arcs.steering: Keep a DJ-mixable intro/outro and make the second drop change one prominent musical feature.
Make the rhythm section carry the drop and make the second drop change the instrumental hook or drum density.
Introduce the core motif early; keep one clear contrast passage before the final return.
Let the emotional motif remain audible in both low- and high-energy passages; change orchestration and rhythm around it.

quality_steering: Make every layer earn its place through a distinct register, rhythm, transient, or harmonic role.
Change one or two foreground ideas at each 8- or 16-bar boundary; keep a recognizable motif through the changes.
Use the smallest number of simultaneous bass roles that creates the desired groove; separate sub weight from mid-bass articulation.
For club_drive, ensure the kick, bass, and hats create forward motion even when the lead is muted; use the lead to make the groove memorable, not to replace it.
Keep a fast, repeatable instrumental motif audible across the drop; automate filter, octave, or answering notes for development without changing the motif beyond recognition.
Let section energy change through note density, register, sustain, and percussion activity as well as loudness.
Treat these rules as review prompts. A deliberate exception can be musically right; listen and compare alternatives.
